title: Operational observability, backup, restore and incident response — agent-panel evaluation

panel_protocol.limitation: Source-verified evaluation of operational contracts, telemetry policies, backup manifests, incident records, reference recovery rehearsals, and resilience workflows; compiler-backed failure injection runs, KMS-encrypted clean-room restore rehearsals, and operational disaster drills remain open gates.

consensus_summary: The multidisciplinary expert evaluation panel reached unanimous consensus approving Track 33 (Operational observability, backup, restore and incident response). The core operational assets—including crates/searchright-ops/src/lib.rs, crates/searchright-ops/tests/policy_failure_injection.rs, crates/searchright-contracts/src/ops.rs, contracts/examples/component-health.json, contracts/examples/telemetry-policy.json, contracts/examples/backup-manifest.json, contracts/examples/incident-record.json, docs/operations/reliability.md, docs/operations/backup-restore.md, docs/operations/incident-response.md, scripts/recovery_rehearsal.py, verification/recovery/rehearsal.json, docs/operations/recovery-reference-rehearsal.md, .github/workflows/resilience.yml, and tests/test_operational_reliability_governance.py—demonstrate exceptional architectural rigor, fail-closed policy design, and strict privacy protection. Component health contracts separate liveness from readiness, requiring components to be Healthy or Degraded to declare readiness, while searchright-ops::readiness rejects empty inputs and transparently exposes degraded components without masking. Telemetry is disabled by default with 0 sampling and 0 retention; enabled telemetry strictly requires an endpoint and human approver, while query_text, full_text, api_key, and personal_identifier are strictly prohibited and enforced via triple-gate authorisation. Backups are content-addressed using SHA-256 and mandate encryption with key references only; unencrypted restores and unauthorised operators are rejected fail-closed. Deterministic reference recovery rehearsal demonstrates atomic replacement, stale temporary isolation, restore idempotency, and cryptographic tamper detection network-free. Incident response enforces structured containment, data exposure tracking, and mandatory postmortems for high/critical incidents, while upholding evidence preservation. All 6 governance unit tests and failure-injection tests pass deterministically. The three higher-evidence operational gates remain preserved as open in the evidence ledger.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Component health contracts, liveness vs readiness segregation, degraded operational modes, fail-closed readiness aggregation, default-disabled telemetry, 0 sampling/retention defaults, and strict prohibition of query_text, full_text, api_key, and personal_identifier verified in source contracts and test suites.

Encrypted backup manifest contracts, key reference isolation, fail-closed unencrypted restore blocking, atomic file replacement, restore idempotency, and cryptographic tamper detection verified in deterministic reference rehearsals.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Incident record contract, mandatory containment, data exposure tracking, postmortem mandates for high/critical incidents, task cancellation doctrine, failure-as-abstention, and CI workflow hardening verified.
